Full program title:
MarijuanaNews World Report for May 12, 2005 LA Times Still Has Not Reported Club Raid; Narks Attack Clubs, But There Will Be No Cannabis In Alameda Hospital. New York Times Still Has Not Reported Prospect Of State Medical Cannabis Law. Farce In The Philippines and the UK.

One way or another, the supply of medical cannabis will remain in the black market until cannabis is fully legalized..

Especially in West Hollywood where a club was the target of a massive police raid last Friday, which still has not been reported in the LA Times, even though the raid involved as many as 50 heavily armed police.

Excerpted from Ryan Gierach's report in the West Hollywood news website: the targeted club, Compassionate Caregivers at 1209 N. La Brea Ave and commonly known as the Yellow House, had been under surveillance by LAPD since September 2004 after the arrest of a Compassionate Caregiver patron with 60 marijuana plants in his possession, all allegedly purchased at Yellow House.

After an eight-month investigation, LAPD narco squad officers and Federal Internal Revenue (IRS) agents raided the medical cannabis club, arresting 14 people and seizing 800 pounds of marijuana product (wholesale value, $2.5 million; retail value over $5 million) and between $300-500,000 in cash...

According to LAPD spokesperson Sgt. Plow, that surveillance found that the club allegedly sold large amounts of marijuana to customers on a regular, sometimes daily, basis. State law forbids the sale of more than eight ounces of medical marijuana to a patient at one time.
(MarijuanaNews note: The state law in question is SB 420, which is almost certainly a violation of the California state constitution because it tries to modify a voter passed initiative Prop 215, which has no such limits.

The American Medical Marijuana Association and Denis Peron opposed SB 420 because they claimed it would be abused by the narks for arbitrary attacks on clubs.)
See
 Davis Makes SB 420 The Law For Now. California Medical Cannabis Movement Split, But So Are The Narks. Analysis by Richard Cowan
and links

We formed the opinion that the club was in violation of Health & Safety Code 11360 (transportation, distribution or importation of controlled substances) through the surveillance, Sgt. Plows told WeHoNews.com.

They regularly sold 8 ounce and one pound quantities to people who made sometimes daily buys. There were an average of 235 visits a day to the house. That's drug dealing, not medicine dispensing.

Acknowledging that the IRS had been involved in the months long investigation, Sgt. Plow said, The key to [IRS involvement] in this raid was the money-laundering investigation [the IRS] is conducting into these businesses. This one was obviously set up for profit, and the law says they should be non-profit.
(MarijuanaNews note: Really?? SB 420 in 11362.765. (a)simply says, nor shall anything in this section authorize any individual or group to cultivate or distribute marijuana for profit. It is the way of totalitarian societies that anything that is not specifically allowed is forbidden.

And are profits un-American?? Tell Merck. Don't tell Bush.)

LAPD arrested employees and patrons en masse and charged 13 people with felony counts of H&SC 11366 (maintaining a place for selling, giving, using controlled substances); one man allegedly holding 21 grams of marijuana but no letter of recommendation identifying him as a medicinal marijuana user was charged with a misdemeanor count of possession.
(MarijuanaNews note: There is supposed to be a state registration system, with ID cards for patients, but the state has not yet complied.
See
 http://www.norml.org/index.cfm?Group_ID=4525&wtm_view=medical

Selective compliance by the police threatens everyone's freedom.)
See
 Selective Enforcement Versus Selective Compliance 2 Articles

As to LAPD's plans to crack down on the other six clubs still operating in West Hollywood, Sgt Plow told WeHoNews that no other clubs, so far as she had been told, were under surveillance by LAPD.

That doesn't mean they aren't surveilling, it only means they don't tell me what they are doing, she said. This surveillance began with a lead from another arrest; LAPD has no plans to raid other clubs [in West Hollywood].

According to Kristin Cook of the city's public safety staff, such inter-jurisdictional investigations are quite common, especially in drug cases. This case was unusual because the gentleman's agreement that exists between agencies about prior notification of a major raid didn't happen, she said. The city and the [Sheriff's] station are displeased at the short notice we received.
(MarijuanaNews note: Of course, the real problem is that as Dr. Lester Grinspoon argues real medical access to cannabis will only be possible with full legalization.
See

and

and

There are almost 10 million people in Los Angeles county. San Francisco city and county has only 750,000 people, and yet it has over 40 clubs. That would mean that LA needs at least 500 clubs! There should be at least 1,500 throughout the state.

When that huge demand is forced through just a few clubs, those clubs are naturally going to do a huge business and need a huge inventory. Clubs like this one might also serve as a wholesaler to smaller clubs.

If the Feds and the local narks won't play by the rules, then how is the system going to work. The short answer is that it will not.)

 Program Notes for the MarijuanaNews World Report for May 9, 2005: Police Raid LA Club. Cannabis in Hospital? Hemp Fails In N. H.; No Recrim In Alaska? Father To Hang In Singapore. Support For Decrim.

Even Sheriff Charles Plummer called it a brilliant idea, but the county supervisors ran into the fact that Fairmont is a public institution and receives federal funds through Medicare and other programs, which they cannot afford to lose and the Feds could arrest the hospital staff and administrators. County Supervisor Scott Haggerty says he is not apt to endorse such a clinic unless Congress approves it. Fat chance!

Meanwhile in New York, the NY Times says that it reports All The News That Is Fit To Print, but so far that has not included attempts to pass a state medical cannabis law.

Based on reports from The New York Daily News and other papers yesterday

The New York state Senate and Assembly could be nearing a joint agreement to allow doctors to prescribe marijuana to seriously ill or dying patients.

Senate Republican Leader Joe Bruno (R-Rensselaer ) was described by his spokesman yesterday as being " open and receptive " to backing medicinal pot.

But Republican Gov. George Pataki is not onboard. A Pataki spokesman said the governor believes there are already legal alternatives available for pain relief. Previously, Pataki had tried to tie an increase cannabis penalties to a bi-partisan effort to ameliorate the state's harsh Rockefeller drug laws. Fortunately, he failed.

The state Health Department spokesman William VanSlyke is quoted as saying, " Our experts ... indicate there are legal medications available that provide the same medical benefit as marijuana.
See
 In Their Own Words: FDA Press Release On New Anti-Nausea Drug For Chemotherapy Patients Prove Prohibitionists Are Lying About Need For Medical Cannabis.
and links

Lawmakers wouldn't speculate Tuesday on whether they could rally the two-thirds vote necessary to override a potential Pataki veto.

Supporters also included representatives from the state Medical Society, the state Nurses' Association and the deans of the state's 15 medical schools.

Now consider this statement by Jo Weiderhorn, executive director of the Associated Medical Schools of New York State:

" The use of marijuana for medical purposes is scientifically established. The deans of New York's medical schools recognize this and support efforts in the Legislature to make marijuana available to patients under the supervision of a doctor. "

Here are three gems excerpted from various Philippine papers:

Fund problems threaten drive vs marijuana

Legal and protocol questions on fund realignment are threatening to derail President Macapagal-Arroyo's proposed projects to wipe out marijuana plantations in two Cordillera towns.

Alquiza, in his report, said the government had already awarded the flyover project to a contractor and it was left with no option but to honor its obligation to fulfill the terms of the contract.

He added that the location of the marijuana-producing barangays in the two towns and the absence of electricity would make it difficult to build the roads and the cable cars.

He said the government must look for other sources of funds since the projects, he said, " are actually presidential commitments to solve the marijuana problem. "

NEW APPROACH VS. DRUGS SOON

Beginning next month, the police will introduce a new approach in their campaign against the illegal drugs trade after they found out that the number of pushers in the city has not decreased.

Drug Enforcement Section chief George Ylanan told reporters yesterday that an updated watchlist of drug personalities has been compiled based on reports from station commanders.

The data reveals that there are about 200 drug pushers in the city. But the police could not claim progress in their campaign because new pushers would surface whenever a drug suspect is arrested.

The new approach against drug pushers in the city was agreed during a meeting with Councilor Augustus Jun Pe, who heads the council committee on dangerous drugs.

It will be patterned after the one being used by the United States Drug Enforcement Agency.

As this developed, intelligence reports revealed that the price of shabu (meth) has significantly decreased with five grams which used to be at P16,000 to P28,000 last November can now be bought at P8,000.

Inmates found planting marijuana in Lumbia jail

ASSISTANT City Fiscal Gregorio Borja said Thursday they are now poised to formally file charges against inmates of the Lumbia City Jail for planting marijuana in jail cells.

The " green-thumb inmates " are reportedly members of the dreaded Batang Mindanao 29 (BM-29).

Records provided by the City Prosecutor's Office showed that sometime at 2 p.m. of March 31, 2004, Lumbia jail guards conducted a surprise raid of the compound following reports from inmates that marijuana is being planted inside the cells.

During the raid they recovered three uprooted marijuana plants grown with vegetables at the garden and another one planted in a tin can. The marijuana plants were already two months old and had grown a foot long.

The jail guards searched every corner of the cells and recovered bladed weapons like improvised arrows or " indian pana " and one cellphone smuggled by the visitor of one of the inmates.

Conspiracy

Prison official Ernesto B. Abella Sr. said the discovery of the deadly weapons confirmed earlier reports the prisoners were planning to stage a disturbance at the jail.

When the seven inmates were brought to the Office of the City Prosecutor for the inquest investigation they denied planting marijuana inside the compound.

But even in the most advanced countries.

Excerpted from Simon Goodley's Diary in The Guardian
Thursday May 12, 2005

" How can an idiot be a policeman? " Dreyfus asks Clouseau in The Return of the Pink Panther. " It's very simple, " he replies. " All he has to do is enlist. " It's an old gag which has proved accurate so often that it's now more of an unofficial recruitment slogan, but we'll add another case file to the in-tray with this tale of bungling law enforcement officers at HM Customs. We begin the story a year ago with a triumph: the seizure of a tonne of cannabis found hidden between sacks of imported washing powder. Customs has a policy of selling or giving away the stuff it confiscates (the soap, not the dope), and in this case 100 charities got help making their whites whiter.
See
 UK Customs Told To Concentrate On Hard Drugs But Deny They Will Be " Soft " On Cannabis Smugglers.

One homeless group in Liverpool received its batch last week, only to discover five kilos of cannabis resin when they opened the bag. Naturally, Customs is far too grand to return our calls inquiring if any of their super-sleuths considered taking a peep inside the sacks, or possibly they're just too busy to ring back. Urgent letters have now been dispatched to the other 99 charities asking if they could please have their hash back. Good luck with that one.
